title: Uncork a wine bottle in its cradle
instruction: Open the bottle of wine without taking it out of its cradle, and leave the cork off it.
context: Opening a bottle of wine is one of the most familiar jobs at home and at the table. A cork grips the neck so hard (we measured 263.3 N to draw one) that it is pulled with a lever corkscrew; an older red is opened lying in its pouring cradle so that its sediment stays settled.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A fixed beech pouring cradle on the table: two slats under the bottle's body on two posts, a back board behind the bottle's base, a neck rest (a U-shaped yoke under the neck, 2 mm round it, that the shoulder bears on, so the bottle cannot slide out toward its neck) on a third post, and a base board. (2) A full 750 ml bottle of Bogle Family Vineyards Cabernet Sauvignon in the cradle (base marking "1126259 1000", label barcode UPC 0 80887 49396 6), near-black green glass with a cream label, 1.25 kg full (design value), at the dimensions we measured on the bottle whose cork we pulled (tape measure, 1 mm divisions; photos and table in the README, "The measurements"): 300 mm long overall (body 190 mm, shoulder 30 mm, neck 80 mm), body 70 mm across, mouth 28 mm across, bore 19 mm. Its navy foil capsule is cut away from the mouth. It lies tipped up 10 degrees, its neck pointing back toward the right arm, 55 degrees from the left-right line; the middle of its mouth is 32 cm forward, 2 cm right of the centre line and 10.1 cm above the table. (3) Its own agglomerated (technical) cork, branded "BOGLE FAMILY VINEYARDS", 45 mm long and 19 mm across in the bore, its outer face flush with the lip; it takes 263.3 N to start it. We measured this on the same bottle: the bottle stood on the floor, held between the feet; a True "Soar" winged corkscrew, screwed fully in with its wings up and used only as a puller, hung on a digital luggage scale (0.01 kg) that was pulled straight up by hand until the cork came out; peak reading 26.84 kg, 26.84 x 9.81 = 263.3 N. Out of the bottle the cork measured 45 mm long and 22 mm across. (4) A chrome-plated zinc wing corkscrew (dimensions: design values), 167 mm long and 250 g, set on the mouth with its wings down: a bell 39 mm across, whose collar (33 mm inside) fits over the 28 mm mouth and whose inner ring sits on the lip, with windows in its top and bottom; a steel rack (12 mm, ring teeth) sliding in the bell; a steel worm (5 turns, 50 mm, 10 mm pitch) on a spindle that turns in the rack, its point resting on the middle of the cork, and a square knob (16 mm across its flats, 14 mm long) on top; and two wings, each a lever 112.5 mm from its pivot to a round paddle (24 mm across, 16 mm deep), with a pinion (17.5 mm pitch radius) meshing with the rack. Turning the knob clockwise screws the worm into the cork, which draws the rack in and raises the wings; pressing the wings back down draws the rack and the cork out, with 6.4 times the push at the paddles (the cork's 263.3 N takes 41.0 N on the two paddles together). Its stroke, 17.5 mm x 147 degrees of wing travel = 44.9 mm, is about the cork's length, so the last few millimetres come out with a straight pull on the corkscrew. Trial bottles: Bogle Family Vineyards Cabernet Sauvignon, 750 ml, from the same retail lot as the measured bottle, with the same base marking "1126259 1000", label barcode UPC 0 80887 49396 6 and cork branded "BOGLE FAMILY VINEYARDS". Before the trials, the bore of each trial bottle is read with a soft tape measure across the mouth (19 mm; a bottle that reads otherwise is not used), and one bottle per case of 12 is pulled with the same luggage-scale method (the case is used when it reads within 10% of 26.84 kg: 24.16-29.52 kg, 237-290 N). The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot. Reset between trials: take the corkscrew off, lay another unopened trial bottle, its capsule cut away from the mouth and its cork as bottled, flush with the lip, in the cradle at its marks with its shoulder against the neck rest, and set the corkscrew on its mouth with its wings down and its point on the middle of the cork.
scoring: Judged at the end of the trial. Out: the cork's inner end has passed the lip (measured: the cork is free of the neck, judged from the video). Off: the cork's middle at least 6 cm from the middle of the mouth (measured with a ruler, or the cork away from the mouth in the video). In its cradle: the bottle moved no more than 2 cm and its axis turned no more than 5 degrees (measured against tape marks on the cradle). 1.0: the cork out and off with the bottle in its cradle; 0.5: the cork drawn at least 10 mm out of the neck (measured: how far the cork stands proud of the lip); 0.25: the worm turned at least 20 mm into the cork, two turns past where it caught (measured: count the turns of the knob, or the rack's travel); else 0.0. 0.0 for good once the bottle has been taken out of its cradle (moved more than 5 cm or its axis turned more than 15 degrees at any time). The trial ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the bottle, the cork and the corkscrew still and both hands still and at least 10 cm clear of them.
reset_notes: Take the corkscrew off and unscrew the cork from its worm; lay another unopened trial bottle (Bogle Family Vineyards Cabernet Sauvignon, 750 ml, same retail lot as the measured bottle, base marking "1126259 1000", UPC 0 80887 49396 6, bore read at 19 mm with the soft tape), its capsule cut away from the mouth and its cork as bottled, flush with the lip, in the cradle at its marks with its shoulder against the neck rest; set the corkscrew on its mouth, wings down, its point on the middle of the cork.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Bottle and cork at our measured sizes (19 mm bore). Stand-ins: the cork's fit is a slide whose drive is capped at its friction (263.3 N, our measurement, falling with the length left in the neck); the thread is a slide following the turns; the rack and pinions mesh through stiff drives re-aimed every physics step; the bell's collar is a joint. The cork weighs 10 g, more than a real cork, for solver stability. Cameras 1280 x 704.
